comparison: Strong agreement on X-ray diffraction findings (C50-C58). Both evaluations support the structural evidence showing myosin head states during torpor. OpenEval notes the I1,1/I1,0 ratio data and considers the OFF-state interpretation reasonable; peer reviewers accept the findings with only minor interpretive caveats about potential disconnect between ATP kinetics and structural movements.

Strong agreement on ATP turnover findings (C3, C34-C47, C86). Both evaluations support the quantitative data showing decreased ATP turnover times and increased consumption during hibernation. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and adequate sample sizes; peer reviewers describe findings as 'valid and interesting' and 'especially interesting,' acknowledging the unexpected nature without challenge.

Strong agreement on temperature-dependent experiments (C4, C59-C64, C87-C88, C104). Both evaluations support the differential responses at 8°C vs 20°C. OpenEval notes quantitative measurements and opposite effects during torpor vs active states; peer reviewers explicitly praise this analysis as 'especially interesting' with no methodological concerns.

Strong agreement on bear myosin structure preservation (C2, C26-C27, C29, C31-C32). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes adequate sample sizes and replication across species; peer reviewers affirm findings without challenge, noting 'solid methodological approaches' and 'well-performed' experiments.

Agreement on phosphorylation data (C66-C70, C75, C107) but different emphasis. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while noting functional significance relies on computational predictions rather than direct experimental validation. Peer reviewers accept the data and computational simulations without challenge, treating mechanistic interpretation as reasonable speculation.

Strong agreement on proteomics and metabolomics findings (C76-C81, C110-C112, C114). Both evaluations support the comprehensive data. OpenEval emphasizes PCA clustering, differential expression, and gene ontology results; peer reviewers explicitly mention proteomics as a strength with no concerns about methodology or interpretation.

Agreement on major conclusions (C7-C8, C98, C117-C118) with nuanced differences. OpenEval supports C7 and C117 (ATP turnover) strongly but considers C8 and C98 (NST role) more speculative. Peer reviewers accept this as a major conceptual contribution, stating the work 'revealed insights into mechanisms of non-shivering thermogenesis' and treating the overall interpretation as a valuable advance.

Divergent evaluations of mechanistic interpretations (C5-C6). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative hypotheses requiring additional validation beyond ATP turnover measurements. Peer reviewers (R4) accept the phosphorylation mechanism as reasonable speculation without challenge. Peer R3 also addresses C65 and C89, which OpenEval includes in this uncertain evaluation.

Agreement on species-specific differences (C73-C74, C84-C85). OpenEval supports these comparative findings as important negative controls. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these negative findings without raising concerns, treating the contrast between species as part of the accepted narrative about differential adaptations.

Agreement on U. arctos metabolic changes (C82-C83). OpenEval supports these findings as providing comparative context. Peer reviewers accept the proteomics findings broadly, with no specific concerns raised about the bear metabolic data.

Partial overlap on PTM findings (C71-C72). OpenEval addresses phosphorylation data and computational predictions; peer reviewers accept the negative findings (no PTMs in bears) implicitly without concerns about methodology or completeness.

Partial overlap on experimental design (C25, C30). OpenEval supports bear fiber measurements; peer reviewers (R9) accept sample sizes and experimental design across both species, noting 'very well-planned study' with only single biopsy site as acknowledged limitation.
Minimal overlap on sample sizes (C33, C41). OpenEval supports the quantitative data from adequate sample sizes; peer reviewers accept the overall experimental design and use of multiple animals.
Minimal overlap on NST interpretation (C119). OpenEval rates mechanistic claims about NST as UNCERTAIN; peer reviewers accept the NST contribution as a major conceptual advance.
Minimal overlap on temperature experiments (C59). OpenEval supports the temperature-dependent data; peer reviewers accept the overall experimental design quality.
Minimal overlap on fiber type adaptation (C90). OpenEval supports preferential type II fiber adaptation based on data; peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall conceptual contribution.

Minimal overlap on mechanistic claims (C65, C89). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN speculative interpretations; peer reviewers accept the temperature-dependent findings that provide context for these claims.
OpenEval addresses assumption about ATP consumption per myosin head (C28) as reasonable based on literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific methodological assumption.

OpenEval rates claims about myosin conformation and atrophy prevention (C93-C94) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative interpretation and hypothetical connections. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific mechanistic hypotheses.

OpenEval rates synthesis of PTM and proteomics findings regarding myosin stability (C116) as UNCERTAIN, noting causal relationships are not directly demonstrated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific mechanistic synthesis.

OpenEval addresses extensive background literature claims (C1, C9-C24, C91-C92, C95-C97, C99-C103, C105, C108-C109) as SUPPORTED established knowledge providing context. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate background claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.
